offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The evidence is consistent from end to end. The webhook was redelivered and queued twice, and the ledger-consumer deployed just before booked both copies.

diagnosis.hypothesis:
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 20:18:28Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 34s before the alert. That handler does not deduplicate by provider event_id.

The provider sent the webhook for evt_000369 (payment.succeeded, pay_000337, $9.68) twice, 0.5s apart, at 20:19:01.185Z and 20:19:01.683Z. Redelivery is normal at-least-once behaviour. webhook-receiver queued each copy, at provider-events partition 1 offsets 155 and 156.

The naive ledger handler posted both copies as separate transactions, 369 and 372. The ledger stays balanced, but provider_clearing for pay_000337 shows $19.36 against the provider's $9.68. That is the +$9.68 drift and the posted_exactly_once failure.

Our payments and refunds tables still agree with the provider, so payment-confirmer is not implicated. Still open: why the provider redelivered so quickly, and what LEDGER_HANDLER the service ran before. The deploy log shows only the current setting, which I infer was an idempotent handler.

evidence.shows: money_check, settled: evt_000369 for pay_000337 ($9.68) was posted 2 times (transactions 369 and 372). Ledger is +$9.68 vs provider. Ledger balanced. Payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer redeployed at 20:18:28Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, the only change after the 20:17:01Z stack start. Other services' settings look normal.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000369 twice, from offsets provider-events/1@155 and @156, under different trace ids. No dedupe was applied.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000369 twice (offsets 155 and 156), so the provider delivered it twice. The duplicate entered Kafka legitimately.

proposed_fix.summary:
Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous settings, presumably the idempotent handler that dedupes on event_id, to stop new double postings.

After that, a reviewed data repair is needed: reverse the duplicate ledger transaction 372 for evt_000369 / pay_000337 with a compensating entry. Then rerun the money check and look for any further duplicates posted while the naive handler ran.

diagnosis.blast_radius:
During the restart, ledger-consumer pauses and lag on provider-events builds up briefly. Nothing is lost, because its consumer group resumes from committed offsets.

If the previous setting were also non-idempotent, the duplicates would continue. The money check would show that.

The rollback does not fix the $9.68 already booked twice. That needs the separate data repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive and BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, the current settings shown in c2. Then confirm it is healthy and consuming.
